prerequisites: an introduction to computer organization and structure

learning_outcomes.text: describe the basic principles of databases;
describe the relational implementation model and convert a conceptual schema into an implementation schema;
work practically with relational query languages, especially with SQL;
make the connection between a database and a program;
identify when and in what way indexes are useful;
identify the ways in which query optimization is important;
explain principles of query processing, data security, database distribution;
explain some techniques and applications (such as data warehouses, data mining)

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Why databases?, general concepts about data and information, files versus databases, database models; concepts about data modeling.
the entity-relationship model and the enhanced entity-relationship model
modeling using the ER and EER model
basic concepts: entities, attributes, tuples, relational database, null values, keys, foreign keys; integrity; description of a relational database;
mapping of an E(E)R schema to a relational schema
relational languages: classification of relational languages, relational algebra, tuple calculus, domain calculus, SQL.
defining and executing queries on a relational database;
accessing a relational database from a program.
dependencies: functional dependencies, multivalued dependencies, join dependencies, general dependencies
vertical decomposition: lossless decomposition, dependency-preserving decompositions; normalization: the normal forms: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, 4NF, 5NF, and the associated decompositions.
details of B- and B+-tree indexes / properties of B/B+ tree indexes
concepts about query optimization, estimation of query cost, optimization of queries.
Design and implementation of a relational database
Working with SQL: table definition, constraints,...
Working with SQL: queries and views
Binding a program with a database
assessment_rules: The evaluation consists of a written exam during the examination period coupled with a portion of continuous assessment during the semester. The written exam is closed book. A formula sheet with SQL syntax will be provided. The exam is a combination of open questions, closed questions, and multiple-choice questions. The continuous assessment includes a midterm test and an assignment. The score for the continuous assessment is carried over to the third examination period but is not carried over to the next academic year.
bibliography: R. Elmasri and S.B. Navathe, "Fundamentals of Database Systems", Pearson (multiple editions can be used).
Slides and other materials made available online.
